source.title: Memory as a cache: Exact context reuse and deletion by construction

record.tranche_reason: The study does not fit scaling laws, but it tests related claim versions by comparing matched-parameter architectures and reporting downstream scores across model scales.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out perplexities at several parameter scales, but does not fit loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute power laws, test small-run extrapolation, or identify compute-optimal allocations. Its architecture comparisons and zero-shot task scores bear on V4 and V6. Other scaling-law statements in the paper are not reported as its own tests.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper (SMem) that fits no scaling law. It still yields two narrow results on claim versions. (1) A depth-matched transformer (10 layers, widened FFN, exact parameter match) reaches nearly the same perplexity as the standard 12-layer one, which bears on V4. (2) Zero-shot accuracy at 160M, 410M and 1.5B (≈20:1 token budgets) bears on V6. The SMem-vs-transformer and RoPE comparisons are between different architecture families, not shape changes, so they do not bear on V4. The Hoffmann 20:1 ratio is used as a tool to set budgets, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SMem reaches perplexity comparable to a parameter-matched transformer, a gap of −4.7% to +2.8% across two recipes and an LR search at 160M–1.5B. In exchange it gains a cache that composes, deletes and edits exactly, and that retrieves beyond the trained length under the shared recipe. The recipe moves the transformer more than the architecture separates the arms. Zero-shot results are at parity on four of five tasks, with LAMBADA favouring SMem.
record.recipe_differences: This is an architectural pretraining comparison, not a scaling-law fitting or extrapolation study. It reports matched-parameter loss comparisons, selected recipe and learning-rate changes, and zero-shot evaluations.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation perplexity differences change with the training recipe: Regime 1 favors SMem, while Regime 2 favors the learned-position transformer. The reported gap also changes with learning-rate choice.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched parameters, changing the architecture family or positional scheme moves perplexity by more than a few percent. SMem vs transformer ranges from −4.7% to +2.8%. A CEPE-style reader trails SMem by 9.7%. A RoPE transformer leads the learned-position one by 5.5–13.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, non-shape architecture choices (positional scheme, attention topology) can change pretraining loss by 5–14%, unlike shape choices.

fits_no_version.finding: A pilot width ladder predicted SMem's perplexity deficit would shrink to at most ~2% at 410M. The outcome inverted the sign (−4.4%), and the recipe (warmup/LR) later moved the transformer by 10.2% at 410M, more than the architecture contrast.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extrapolating architecture gaps from small pilots is fragile, and recipe choices can dominate architecture contrasts at fixed parameters.

record.problems: The paper does not fit scaling laws or test extrapolation. The largest-scale perplexity comparison is a single seed pair; the 410M comparisons use two seeds. The zero-shot uncertainty is item-sampling only, and the 1.5B results use one seed.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported V4 or V6 results were left out.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute; only three scales (160M–1.5B).
No fitted law extrapolated to larger runs. The only registered extrapolation concerns the SMem/transformer gap, not loss.
No fixed-compute sweep; the 20:1 tokens-per-parameter ratio is adopted from Hoffmann et al. as a tool.
Only one shape variant (12→10 layers with widened FFN, 160M, Regime 1). No wide depth/width sweep and no other scales.
No fit of downstream score to scale or loss, and no prediction from small to large models. Only three scales; 1.5B is a single seed.
No exponents or compute-optimal splits fitted or compared.

missing.what: Symmetric learning-rate search at 160M: both arms move by 10–11% over LR 9e-4 to 2.2e-3 while the SMem/transformer contrast stays at +2.4% to +2.8%. This is relevant to recipe sensitivity, not to a listed version.
A 7-layer memory-free transformer (127.7M) reads 29.29 vs 26.51 for the 12-layer one under Regime 2. Parameters differ, so this is not a fixed-parameter shape test.

record.verdict_notes: Not a scaling-law study; evidence on V4 and V6 is incidental and thin. The record's V4 linkage of SMem-vs-transformer rows was over-broad. Those compare architecture families, not shape, so they move to fits_no_version. The record also had wrong HellaSwag 1.5B values (copied from ARC-e) and wrong SMem 160M WinoGrande (0.513, not 0.505). HellaSwag at 160M/410M and all WinoGrande scores are near chance.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit for held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute; the reported scales span 160M–1.5B parameters.
No fits on small runs used to predict the loss of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or fitted compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
The comparisons do not sweep a wide range of depth and width at fixed parameter count; most results concern a small set of architecture variants and training recipes.
No modalities or training regimes beyond text pretraining and the reported zero-shot evaluations.
No fitted relationship between downstream scores and pretraining loss, and no predictive calibration from smaller to larger models.
The paper varies recipes and learning rates but does not fit or compare scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: Depth-matched transformer

rows.baseline: Standard learned-position transformer; numeric baseline not stated in this comparison
rows.uncertainty: Three seeds; gap closure reported as −27%.

relationships.reason: The depth-matched transformer reads 30.09 vs 29.72 for the standard one, about a 1.2% change from a shape change (r12).
relationships.display_finding: The reshaped Transformer had a reported value of 30.09 versus 29.72 for the standard model, a change of about 1.2%.

source_check.reason: Appendix G and Table 2 give 30.09 versus 29.72 perplexity, approximately a 1.2% difference. This supports V4 for this local comparison.

relationships.condition: LAMBADA, ARC-e, PIQA, HellaSwag across 160M, 410M and 1.5B, both architectures
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically with scale on these tasks, e.g. LAMBADA .155→.231→.348 for the transformer and HellaSwag .273→.293→.356 (r20–r43). Only three points and no fit.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased at every tested size on all four tasks, including transformer LAMBADA scores of 0.155→0.231→0.348 and HellaSwag scores of 0.273→0.293→0.356.

relationships.reason: Scores stay near chance and non-monotonic (T .505/.502/.518; S .513/.509/.508), so no improvement with scale appears at these sizes (r44–r49).
relationships.display_finding: Transformer scores were 0.505, 0.502 and 0.518, while SMem scores declined through 0.513, 0.509 and 0.508, showing no consistent gains from 160M to 1.5B.
